questions.question: In function calling, what exactly is a "tool"?
options: A plugin pre-installed inside the model, run directly by the model
A list of function declarations shipped with each request; the function bodies stay in your application
A snippet of executable code the model generates on the spot from the question
The function's source code pasted into the prompt
questions.explanation: See the "Tools are a list of function declarations shipped with the request" section: a tool is not a plugin installed into the model but a declaration sent with each request, and the model never touches real code — the function bodies stay in your application forever.

questions.question: What does the model actually output when it "calls a tool"?
options: A structured tool_use request; your client code performs the actual execution
The result of the tool, already executed
The tool's name, description and input_schema triplet
A query command with the database credentials attached
questions.explanation: See the "The model emits a request, not an execution" section: the model outputs a tool_use block with type, id, name and input and sets stop_reason to tool_use to say "I am waiting for the result" — execution authority always stays on the client.

questions.question: In a tool_result block, what is tool_use_id for?
options: To mark whether the execution succeeded or failed
To record the token cost of the call
To pair with the request's id so the model knows which result answers which request
To identify which tool function produced the result
questions.explanation: See the "The reply: tool_result paired by id" section: tool_use_id must pair with the request's id — when several requests are in flight, the id is the only way to know which result answers which request.
